control_flow: avoidWalls: if the right light is below 60 % (dim), then if an obstacle is ahead turn left 15°, else if an obstacle is on the left turn right 15°, else driveInTheDark; if not dim, driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light is below 70 % (dim), drive forward at 30 %; else stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: In a dark tunnel, steer away from its walls: turn right when a wall is close on the left, turn left when one is close on the right, and get through a bending tunnel without touching it.

decision_points.condition: the right light sensor is below 60 % (dim on the right)

branches.outcome: dim: it looks at the obstacle sensors
bright: it goes on to driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: first: an obstacle is ahead; second: an obstacle is on the left

branches.outcome: an obstacle is ahead: it turns left 15°
no obstacle ahead, an obstacle on the left: it turns right 15°
no obstacle ahead or on the left: it goes on to driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor is below 70 % (dim on the left)

branches.outcome: bright: it goes on to stopAtWall
an obstacle is ahead: it stops
no obstacle ahead: it goes on to followLine

scenarios.coded_response: It reads only the left obstacle sensor, never the right one, so it keeps driving forward until the wall stands in front of its front sensor, and then turns left 15°

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left on black and right on the floor

scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end

uncertainties: Your program never reads the right obstacle sensor, so a wall close on the right is only noticed once it stands in front of the front sensor: in a bend to the left it turns left only then.
A wall that stands straight ahead in the dark makes the program turn left (D2.1), which you didn't describe.
In bright light (not in a tunnel) the program goes on to stop at a wall and otherwise to follow a line; you didn't describe that part, so those scenarios are taken from the program.
In bright light on a plain floor the program curves right without end, so a test in bright light has to start on a line or in front of a wall.
